Title: Letter from the CEO
Text: 2025 was a year of growth for Marlow & Finch. Revenue reached a record €48.6 million, driven by new wholesale contracts with hotel groups and three new cafés in Antwerp and Leuven. Green coffee prices rose sharply during the year, which put pressure on our margins, but our pricing actions position us well for 2026. Our balance sheet remains strong and we continue to invest in growth. I want to thank our 212 employees for their dedication. — Sofie Marlow, CEO

Title: About the company
Text: Marlow & Finch Coffee Roasters NV is a specialty coffee company founded in 2011 in Ghent, Belgium. The company roasts about 2,900 tonnes of coffee per year at its roastery in Ghent. It sells through three channels: Wholesale (hotels, restaurants and offices), Cafés (17 company-owned cafés in Flanders) and Online (subscriptions and web shop). The financial year runs from 1 January to 31 December.

Title: Key figures
Text: Key figures (€ thousand), 2025 vs 2024. Revenue: 48,600 vs 42,300. Gross profit: 17,500 vs 16,900. Operating profit (EBIT): 3,900 vs 5,200. Net profit: 2,140 vs 3,300. Employees at year-end: 212 vs 188. Number of cafés: 17 vs 14.

Title: Income statement
Text: Income statement (€ thousand), 2025 vs 2024. Revenue: 48,600 vs 42,300. Cost of sales: (31,100) vs (25,400). Gross profit: 17,500 vs 16,900. Operating expenses: (13,600) vs (11,700). Operating profit (EBIT): 3,900 vs 5,200. Net finance costs (Note 10): (1,050) vs (800). Profit before tax: 2,850 vs 4,400. Income tax: (710) vs (1,100). Net profit: 2,140 vs 3,300. Operating expenses include depreciation and amortisation of €2,100 thousand (2024: €1,900 thousand).

Title: Revenue by channel
Text: Revenue by channel (€ million), 2025 vs 2024. Wholesale: 27.2 vs 23.0. Cafés: 15.1 vs 12.9. Online: 6.3 vs 6.4. Total: 48.6 vs 42.3. Online subscriptions declined slightly as some customers cancelled after the price increase.

Title: Cost of sales and coffee prices
Text: Cost of sales rose to €31.1 million (2024: €25.4 million), or 64.0% of revenue compared with 60.0% a year earlier. The main cause was the price of green arabica beans, which averaged 38% higher than in 2024 after poor harvests in Brazil and Vietnam. This was the main reason operating profit fell. The company had hedged about 40% of its 2025 bean needs at fixed prices; the remaining 60% was bought at market prices. Energy costs for roasting fell by 6%.

Title: Pricing and volumes
Text: To offset higher bean costs, Marlow & Finch raised its selling prices by an average of 9% on 1 April 2025. Volumes sold grew by 5%, mainly from new wholesale contracts. Because the price increase only took effect in April, it covered the higher costs only partly during the year. Management expects the full-year effect to support operating margins in 2026.

Title: Operating expenses
Text: Operating expenses increased to €13.6 million (2024: €11.7 million). Staff costs rose by €1.2 million because of 24 additional employees for the new cafés and wage indexation of 3.6%. Depreciation and amortisation was €2.1 million (2024: €1.9 million). Rent for the three new cafés added €0.4 million.

Title: Balance sheet summary
Text: Balance sheet summary (€ thousand, at 31 December), 2025 vs 2024. Total assets: 41,800 vs 36,500. Equity: 15,600 vs 14,300. Borrowings: 19,400 vs 15,200. Cash: 2,000 vs 3,100. Net debt (borrowings − cash): 17,400 vs 12,100.

Title: Note 14 – Borrowings
Text: The company has a €14.0 million term loan and a €12.5 million revolving credit facility with its bank. At 31 December 2025, €5.4 million of the credit facility was drawn. Interest is charged at Euribor plus 2.25%. Interest expense on borrowings was €1.3 million in 2025 (2024: €0.95 million). The loan agreement includes a financial covenant: net debt may not exceed 3.0 times EBITDA, tested on 30 June and 31 December. At 31 December 2025 the ratio was 2.9x (2024: 1.7x).

Title: Note 10 – Net finance costs
Text: Net finance costs (€ thousand), 2025 vs 2024. Interest expense on borrowings: (1,300) vs (950). Interest income on deposits: 250 vs 150. Net finance costs: (1,050) vs (800).

Title: Risk management
Text: The main risks for the company are green coffee price volatility, competition in the specialty coffee market and dependence on key wholesale customers. Liquidity risk is considered low: the company has a long-standing relationship with its bank, generates positive operating cash flow and has unused headroom on its credit facility. The company reviews its financial risks every month.

Title: Note 22 – Events after the balance sheet date
Text: On 15 January 2026 Marlow & Finch acquired Café Aurora, a chain of five cafés in Brussels, for €6.5 million, paid from the revolving credit facility. Including Café Aurora, pro forma net debt is €23.9 million and pro forma EBITDA €6.6 million, a ratio of 3.6x. The lenders have agreed to waive the covenant test of 30 June 2026 and replace it with a test on 30 September 2026 at the same 3.0x limit. If the limit is exceeded then, the lenders can demand early repayment of all borrowings.

Title: Outlook 2026
Text: For 2026 management expects revenue growth of 15–20%, including Café Aurora, and a recovery in gross margin as the April 2025 price increase applies for the full year. Green coffee prices remain high. The company plans to open two more cafés.
